questions.q: How have people used events in the sky to measure time?
answer: Since ancient times, people have measured time by watching regularly repeating events in the sky.

answer.text: The day is measured by the rotation of the Earth on its axis, which gives day and night. The month comes from the changing phases of the Moon, one full cycle taking about 29.5 days. The year is measured by the revolution of the Earth around the Sun.

Early people used the sundial, which tells time from the shadow cast by the Sun, and observed the positions of stars. These observations were organised into calendars — lunar calendars based on the Moon, solar calendars based on the Sun, and luni-solar calendars combining both, such as the traditional Indian calendars.

answer: The widely used Gregorian calendar has 365 days, with 366 in a leap year.
